## dependency_form
- Prerequisite sentences: verbatim on the blocked side only; no restatement as an action; no aggregation beyond the hub's own consecutive source sentences; depended-on hubs never mention the share. Hops A/B were state-derived in the blind answer. PASS.
- Titles/openings: general subjects ("Customer's Share Payment", "Customer-Billed Vault Storage", "Declared-Value Coverage Billing", "Storage Days the Carrier Does Not Pay" …); none mirrors the task. PASS.
- **K-1 (KB-EXPLICIT RED): computation documents list inputs only a factor uses.**
  - customer_vault_storage_line_calculation_f44eae72, table "Quantities and where they come from": "The boxes packed | the job record, as recorded at custody start" and "The tier's vault rate, period length and vault capacity". The baseline ("the vault count recorded on the job times the tier's vault rate") uses neither boxes packed nor vault capacity; only the vaults-charged factor (vaults_billed_count) does. The rows tell a reader of the baseline that the vault count may be refigured from boxes and capacity.
  - customer_share_amount_calculation_e158311e, table "Quantities read from the job": "Period length | the tier's storage period length, from the product's storage rate card". The standard share never uses it; only the storage-days factor (uncovered_storage_days, "divided by the tier's period length") does.
  - Root on the source side: S-1 (these are plain bindings in the source compute, used by one factor only). The solution is unaffected; the defect is that the baseline document hints at a variation that should be discovered from the records.
- Observations (source-borne, no KB verdict): the generic combination sentences ("any percentage … any factor … any add per vault … the fraction of the period") are the rules' own assembly sentences (XF A2/A5 form); the return-period factor documents each say the sibling line "follows that rule's own fraction" (S-2, source replaced_by text).
- Verdict: **KB-EXPLICIT RED (K-1)**.
